The same artifact will hit Grid/GridColumn/GridRow when that family is added to this harness, since they also render their root tag via `element`. Applies to every variant, including as-button (button.classes[ember-view]).

Checkbox.reason: @carbon/react's Checkbox wraps its own `cds--checkbox-wrapper` class list with an additional `cds--form-item` (`classnames('cds--checkbox-wrapper', {...}, 'cds--form-item' via the outer wrapperClasses computation) - Ember's checkbox.gts root only ever renders `cds--checkbox-wrapper`. A real, minor gap (affects form-item spacing/layout rules), left as-is since checkbox.gts's structure is otherwise a deliberate, simpler port - see the three structural entries below for the bigger picture. Applies to every variant.

Structural: @carbon/react's Checkbox renders `<input>` as a sibling of `<label>` (both direct children of the wrapper div); Ember's checkbox.gts nests the `<input>` INSIDE the `<label>` instead (a common, simpler, equally-valid HTML pattern for implicitly associating a control with its label - no `for`/`id` pairing is strictly required that way). This one tag-mismatch swallows the rest of the comparison at this position (diffing stops once tags disagree), so Ember's own nested input/label-text structure isn't cross-checked against upstream's - it's verified separately by this addon's own checkbox-test.gts instead. Applies to every variant.

Same structural difference as the `div > input[0]` entry above - upstream's second top-level child (the `<label>`, now that `<input>` occupies index 0) has no separate counterpart in Ember's tree, since Ember's single `<label>` already appears (nested around the input) at index 0. Applies to every variant.

@carbon/react's Checkbox always renders a `cds--checkbox__validation-msg` wrapper div (empty unless `invalid`/`warn` is set) as its third child. Ember's `checkbox.gts` has no `invalid`/`warn`/`helperText` args at all, so it never renders anything at this position - a real, larger API gap (this addon's Checkbox doesn't support upstream's invalid/warn states), out of scope for a DOM-parity-only pass. Applies to every variant.

RadioButton.reason: Same harness limitation as RadioTile's entry of the same name (see that entry in this file) - Glimmer's bound `checked={{this.checked}}` sets the DOM `checked` IDL property, not a reflected HTML attribute, so `normalizeElement` (which only reads real attribute nodes) sees it as absent on the Ember side even though the radio button is genuinely checked.

RadioButtonGroup.reason: Ember's radio-button/group.gts always renders `cds--radio-button-group--{{this.args.orientation}}` (defaulting to 'horizontal'), while @carbon/react's `RadioButtonGroup.js` only conditionally adds this class for the vertical case (`[`${prefix}--radio-button-group--${orientation}`]: orientation === 'vertical'` - it never emits a `--horizontal` variant at all, even though `orientation` defaults to 'horizontal'). Harmless either way (horizontal is the group's default flex layout regardless of this modifier class), but a real, disclosed divergence - fixing it would mean Ember's class list stops being unconditional, out of scope for a one-line fix. Applies to every variant that isn't 'vertical'.

A real, disclosed behavioral divergence: Ember's `RadioButton#labelPosition` getter falls back to `this.args.group?.args.labelPosition`, so every grouped radio button visually inherits the group's `@labelPosition`. Upstream's `RadioButtonGroup.js`'s `getRadioButtons()` never passes `labelPosition` down when cloning children (only `name`/`value`/`onChange`/`checked`/`required`) - each `RadioButton`'s own label position stays at its individual default ('right') regardless of the group's `labelPosition`, which only affects the group's own fieldset-level modifier class. This is the first (name='a') grouped RadioButton.
Same disclosed divergence as the `fieldset > div[1].classes[cds--radio-button-wrapper--label-left]` entry above, for the second (name='b') grouped RadioButton.

A real, disclosed divergence, not a markup bug: upstream's `getRadioButtonsWithWrappers`-style cloning (`RadioButtonGroup.js`) only ever passes `name`/`value`/`onChange`/`checked`/`required` down to each child `RadioButton` - never `disabled` - relying entirely on the surrounding `<fieldset disabled>` to actually disable the inputs. Ember's `RadioButton#disabled` getter falls back to `this.args.group?.args.disabled`, so a grouped input gets an explicit `disabled` attribute in addition to inheriting it from the fieldset. Functionally identical either way (`fieldset[disabled]` already makes every descendant control unfocusable regardless of its own `disabled`/`tabindex`), matching the same call already made for RadioTile/TileGroup - see AGENTS.md's own note on this. This is the first (name='a') grouped RadioButton.
Same disclosed divergence as the `fieldset > div[1] > input[0].attributes.disabled` entry above, for the second (name='b') grouped RadioButton.

Toggle.reason: @carbon/react's Toggle links its `<button role="switch">` to its own label via `aria-labelledby={ariaLabelledby ?? (labelText ? labelId : undefined)}`, where `labelId` is a real, upstream-generated `{id}_label` id on the label element (see the `div > label[1].attributes.id` entry below). Ember's `toggle.gts` has no equivalent wiring - the button and the visible label text are never connected via ARIA at all, even though `@name` is Ember's direct analog of `labelText`. A real, disclosed accessibility gap (screen readers get no accessible name from the label association upstream provides), out of scope for a DOM-parity-only pass. Applies to every variant.

Same gap as the `aria-labelledby` entry above - the `{id}_label` id upstream generates for this exact linking purpose has no counterpart in Ember's `toggle.gts`, which renders its `<label>` with no `id` at all. Applies to every variant.

@carbon/react wraps the visible label text in its own `Text` component (default `as='span'`), which sets `dir='auto'` on itself (see this file's other `Text`-wrapper entries, e.g. Notification's). Ember's `<span class='cds--toggle__label-text'>` is a plain span with no `dir` attribute. Applies to every variant.
Same `Text`-wrapper `dir='auto'` gap as the entry above, on the On/Off side-label span (`cds--toggle__text`) instead of the main label text span. Applies to every variant.

Upstream's Toggle renders a small checkmark `<svg>` inside the switch thumb whenever `size='sm'` (and not `readOnly`) - a real, purely decorative detail of the small variant (`Toggle.js`'s `isSm && !readOnly` branch). Ember's `toggle.gts` has no equivalent - it renders the same empty `cds--toggle__switch` div regardless of size. A real, undocumented-until-now gap, out of scope for a DOM-parity-only pass.

Harness limitation, not a functional gap: Glimmer's bound `value={{this.value}}` on an `<input>` sets the DOM `value` IDL property, not a reflected HTML attribute (the same class of gap already documented for `checked` on RadioTile/RadioButton) - `normalizeElement` only inspects real attribute nodes, so it sees the value as absent on the Ember side even though the input genuinely displays 'Hello'.

Ordering difference, not a missing feature: @carbon/react's TextInput renders `[input, Icon]` (icon after the input) inside the field wrapper, while Ember's text-input.gts renders `{{#if isInvalid}}<WarningFilled/>{{/if}} <input>` (icon before the input). Both icons are positioned via `@carbon/styles`' own absolute positioning, so the swapped DOM order has no visual effect, but the harness's index-based diff sees the two elements at index 0 as different tags.
